subtopics.title: What a Circuit Actually Moves — Charge, Energy and Resistance

questions.question: Which statement defines potential difference correctly?
options: The rate of flow of charge past a point
The work done per unit charge, V = W/Q, measured in joules per coulomb
The opposition a conductor offers to charge flow
The total charge stored in a battery

questions.question: A potential difference of 12 V across a resistor means that:
options: 12 coulombs pass through it every second
the resistor has a resistance of 12 Ω
every coulomb of charge passing through it transfers 12 joules of energy
12 joules of charge are destroyed in the resistor

questions.question: How must an ammeter and a voltmeter be connected?
options: Ammeter in series (low resistance); voltmeter in parallel with the component (high resistance)
Both in series with the component
Ammeter in parallel (high resistance); voltmeter in series (low resistance)
Both in parallel with the battery

questions.question: Why does a battery go flat even though the charge circulating in the circuit is never used up?
options: The coulombs slowly leak out of the wires
Resistance destroys charge as heat
The current gradually turns into voltage
The chemical potential energy that lifts each coulomb's energy is finite; the energy is spent in the resistors as heat and light

subtopics.title: Ohm's Law and the Series Circuit — One Path, Shared Current

questions.question: A 4 Ω and an 8 Ω resistor are connected in series to a 12 V battery. What is the total resistance and the current?
options: 2,67 Ω and 4,5 A
12 Ω and 1 A
12 Ω and 12 A
32 Ω and 0,375 A

questions.question: In that series circuit, the potential differences across the 4 Ω and 8 Ω resistors are:
options: 6 V and 6 V
12 V and 12 V
4 V and 8 V
8 V and 4 V

questions.question: The current in a series circuit is:
options: the same at every point, because there is only one path for charge
shared between the resistors in proportion to their resistance
largest just after the battery and smallest just before it
used up as it passes through each resistor

questions.question: Adding a third resistor in series to an existing series circuit will:
options: raise the current everywhere
leave the current unchanged
raise the total resistance and lower the current everywhere
lower the total resistance below the smallest resistor

subtopics.title: The Parallel Circuit — Shared Potential Difference, Divided Current

questions.question: The 4 Ω and 8 Ω resistors are now connected in parallel across the same 12 V battery. The total resistance is:
options: 6 Ω

questions.question: The currents in the 4 Ω and 8 Ω branches, and the total current, are:
options: 3 A, 1,5 A and 4,5 A
1,5 A, 3 A and 4,5 A
1 A, 1 A and 2 A

questions.question: The potential difference across each of two resistors connected in parallel across a 12 V battery is:
options: 12 V across each, because both branches lie between the same two junctions
6 V across each, because the 12 V is shared equally
8 V and 4 V, split in proportion to the resistances
0 V, because the branches cancel

questions.question: Why is the total resistance of a parallel combination always less than the smallest branch resistance?
options: Because the reciprocals cancel out
Because the branches share the current so each one heats less
Because each extra branch gives the charge another path to flow through, so the combination opposes flow less than any single path
Because the potential difference is divided between the branches

subtopics.title: Series Against Parallel — the Rules, the Traps and the Wiring in Your Walls

questions.question: A learner calculates 1/Rp = 3/8 and writes the answer as 0,375 Ω. What went wrong?
options: Nothing — 0.375 Ω is correct
The reciprocals should have been multiplied
The 12 V should have been divided by 8 first
The answer 3/8 is the reciprocal of the resistance; it must be inverted to give 8/3 = 2,67 Ω

questions.question: Which pairing of rules is correct?
options: Series: same current, potential differences add, resistances add. Parallel: same potential difference, currents add, reciprocals add
Series: same potential difference, currents add. Parallel: same current, potential differences add
Series: reciprocals add. Parallel: resistances add
Both patterns share the current equally between components

questions.question: Household plugs and lights are wired in parallel mainly because:
options: parallel wiring uses less copper
each appliance receives the full supply voltage, and switching one off leaves the others working
parallel wiring draws less total current
parallel wiring prevents the circuit breaker from ever tripping

questions.question: Switching on more appliances in a home has what effect on the circuit as a whole?
options: The total resistance rises and the total current falls
Neither the total resistance nor the current changes
The total resistance falls and the total current rises, which is why an overloaded multiplug overheats and a breaker trips
Each appliance receives a smaller share of the 230 V

questions.question: In the one-road picture, what does the battery actually hand out?
options: New taxis, which are used up along the route
A full load of energy to every bit of charge that passes through it
Resistance, which slows the traffic
Extra roads for the traffic to use

questions.question: On a single road with a 4 Ω rough patch and an 8 Ω rough patch, the traffic flow is:
options: the same at every point on the route
biggest at the smooth patch and smallest at the rough patch
halved by each rough patch
zero after the second patch

questions.question: On that single road with 12 volts driving it, the energy split across the two patches is:
options: 12 V at each patch
6 V and 6 V
4 V at the 4 Ω patch and 8 V at the 8 Ω patch, adding back to 12 V
8 V at the 4 Ω patch and 4 V at the 8 Ω patch

questions.question: When the road splits into a 4 Ω route and an 8 Ω route between the same two corners, the voltage drop on each route is:
options: the full 12 V on both routes
6 V on each route
8 V on one and 4 V on the other
It depends on how many taxis choose each route

questions.question: How does the traffic split between the two routes?
options: Equally, 2,25 A each
3 A on the 4 Ω route and 1,5 A on the 8 Ω route — the easier road is the busier one
1,5 A on the 4 Ω route and 3 A on the 8 Ω route
All of it takes the 8 Ω route

questions.question: The 'upside-down sum' for the two roads gives three-eighths. What must you do next?
options: Multiply by 12 to get the resistance
Nothing — 3/8 Ω is the combined roughness
Flip it back the right way up: 8/3, which is 2,67 Ω
Add it to the 4 Ω and 8 Ω

questions.question: A learner's parallel total comes out bigger than the smallest branch. What is the surest diagnosis?
options: The battery voltage was wrong
The branches must have been in series after all
The current was calculated before the resistance
The fraction was never flipped back the right way up

subtopics.title: Why Your House Is Wired the Clever Way

questions.question: What would go wrong if a house were wired as one single loop?
options: Every appliance would draw too much current
Appliances would share the voltage so all run weakly, and switching one off — or one globe blowing — would kill everything
The total resistance would drop dangerously low
The lights would each get the full 230 V but the plugs would not

questions.question: Which components in a home are deliberately connected in series?
options: The plug points and the lights
The geyser and the fridge
The wall switch and the circuit breaker with the circuit they control
Nothing in a house is ever in series

questions.question: The same 4 Ω and 8 Ω resistors on the same 12 V battery gave 1 A in series and 4,5 A in parallel. The lesson is that:
options: resistors behave differently when they are warm
the battery is stronger in parallel circuits
current always increases with time
the connection pattern, not the components, decides the total resistance and therefore the current
